messages:
Alex - Customer: Hey team — we've been seeing streaming responses over our private VPC break after ~60s. This is using wss to your private endpoint (private-api.redwood.internal). Browser console shows \"WebSocket is closed before the connection is established\" sometimes, other times it opens then drops after ~1m. We're on a restricted egress allowlist and go through a corporate proxy.

Sara (Support): Thanks Alex — sorry you're hitting this. Quick questions: 1) Is this WebSocket (wss) or SSE/chunked HTTP? 2) Any TLS inspection/proxy that could be terminating TLS? 3) Can you repro from a bastion in the same VPC?

Alex - Customer: It's true WebSocket (wss). We also tried server-sent events and saw similar buffering behavior. We can repro from our bastion in the same subnet. No visible TLS errors in app logs — cert chain looks fine to us.

Mike SRE: :eyes: Common culprits in private VPC flows: ALB/NLB idle timeouts, corporate proxy middleboxes doing TLS MITM, or an egress NAT/LSF appliance that's buffering until completion. ALB default idle timeout = 60s which matches your symptom. Are you routing through an ALB?

Alex - Customer: We're behind an internal HTTP proxy that then goes out via a NAT GW > ALB to you. So there are multiple devices in path.

Jen Runtime: Ok. For streaming over HTTP (SSE/chunked) middleboxes sometimes buffer until response complete. For true WebSockets, proxies must allow Upgrade handshake and keep connections open — if any hop enforces a 60s idle window, it'll close. Two quick repro checks:
1) From the bastion run wscat (or ws client) to confirm server behavior:
   npm i -g wscat
   wscat -c \"wss://private-api.redwood.internal/v1/streams/session123\"
   (watch whether connection stays open, then wait 70-90s)
2) Capture packets:
   sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host private-api.redwood.internal -w /tmp/ws.pcap
   Reproduce then share the pcap. Look for FIN/RST or TLS close alerts at ~60s.

Sara (Support): Also, please run these TLS and DNS checks from the bastion:
- DNS: dig +short private-api.redwood.internal @<your-vpc-dns>
- TLS SNI cert check: openssl s_client -connect private-api.redwood.internal:443 -servername private-api.redwood.internal -showcerts
- Curl keep-alive test (for SSE/chunked):
  curl -v -N \"https://private-api.redwood.internal/v1/streams/sse-test\" -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\"
If curl blocks and returns nothing until the server finishes, likely buffering.

Alex - Customer: Ran openssl and the cert CN/SAN is correct; however our proxy is doing outbound TLS inspection and replacing certs (we see its cert as issuer). Could that cause the issue?

Mike SRE: Yes — TLS inspection proxies sometimes terminate TLS, re-establish a new TLS session to upstream, and might not properly forward Upgrade headers or keepalive semantics. If the proxy rewrites headers or buffers responses, streaming breaks. Two paths: a) allow direct egress to our endpoint (bypass MITM for that host), or b) configure proxy to allow WebSocket Upgrade/transparent tunnel.

Jen Runtime: From the server/runtime perspective, verify these on your proxy/nginx/ALB equivalents:
- For nginx fronting clients:
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
  proxy_set_header Connection $http_connection; # or set $connection_upgrade via map
  proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
  proxy_send_timeout 3600s;
  proxy_buffering off;
  chunked_transfer_encoding off;
- For ALB: increase idle timeout (default 60s) or use a TCP-level NLB so the LB won't inject an idle timeout.
- Ensure any WAF/proxy does NOT buffer response bodies for chunked or torn frames.

Alex - Customer: Our proxy is a corporate squid/bluecoat-ish device. I don't have control to change it quickly. Any mitigations we can do on client or server side?

Sara (Support): Short-term mitigations:
- Implement WebSocket-level ping/pong from your client every 20s to keep the connection active (many middleboxes treat idle TCP as idle).
- Add reconnect logic with exponential backoff; resume streams (we support resuming via cursor/token).
- Switch to a TCP-level (NLB) endpoint if you can route to it (avoids HTTP idle timeouts).
- For SSE, ensure server flushes small chunks frequently and sets Transfer-Encoding: chunked and sends \n (LF) after each event so proxies flush.

Mike SRE: Also helpful: capture HTTP headers around handshake to verify Upgrade/Connection headers preserved. From bastion:
   printf 'GET /v1/streams/session123 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: private-api.redwood.internal\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nSec-WebSocket-Key: xxxxx\r\nSec-WebSocket-Version: 13\r\n\r\n' | openssl s_client -connect private-api.redwood.internal:443 -servername private-api.redwood.internal -quiet
Check whether the server returns 101 Switching Protocols and that the proxy doesn't rewrite.

Alex - Customer: We did the openssl raw GET and saw 101 initially, but connection drops at ~60s with no 100/200 or final code. pcap shows FIN from x.x.x.x (our proxy) at 60s.

Jen Runtime: That nails it — proxy is closing the idle connection. If you can't change proxy settings, implement keepalive pings from client, or move to a TCP tunnel. We can also expose a dedicated NLB endpoint for your account for a short period — that'll avoid the HTTP proxy behavior. If you'd like that, we need approval from infra and will schedule change window.

Sara (Support): Next steps for us / info we need from you: 1) Attach pcap and the openssl output. 2) Confirm whether you can bypass proxy for just the Redwood host (policy request). 3) If you want the NLB option, provide the account id and we can open an internal ticket to provision a TCP endpoint.

Alex - Customer: Uploading pcap + openssl output now. We'll also request a bypass but not sure how fast. For now we'll add ping/pong and reconnect. Thanks, please keep this thread updated if NLB is an option.

Mike SRE: Great. If you add pings, aim for 20-25s interval. Also set your client's TCP keepalive (OS) lower than 60s to mirror. We can follow up with the NLB option.

deploy-bot: deployed restart-streaming-prober to staging @ 1763254800 :white_check_mark:

Sara (Support): Thanks Alex — we got the artifacts. I'll open an internal ticket to discuss NLB option and loop in infra. Adding @Jen Runtime and @Mike SRE to the ticket. We'll update here when we have options. :thumbsup:
